properties.name: Newport Pagnell curated visitor boundary
properties.methodology: Morphological closing of the preserved official built-up-area geometry using a 200 metre outward and inward buffer. This fills internal omissions for connected parks, river corridors and visitor green spaces without applying a general outward town buffer.

project.boundarySource: Curated Newport Pagnell visitor boundary derived from ONS Built-up Areas (December 2024)
project.researchNotes: Townscape Guides audit completed 2026-08-09. The unchanged ONS 2024 built-up area is the active inclusion boundary. Historic England designations and public current OpenStreetMap visitor facilities were filtered point-in-polygon. Historic England official list-entry date enrichment completed 2026-08-09: 16 of 102 statutory records now carry defensible date evidence; unresolved entries were individually checked and retained as unknown.

touristAppeal.label: Not a tourist town
touristAppeal.summary: Newport Pagnell has recorded local interest, but its current in-boundary visitor offer does not meet the threshold for a tourist-town rating.

townGuide.headline: An iron bridge, old coaching streets and riverside paths
townGuide.intro: Newport Pagnell rewards a compact heritage walk linking Tickford Bridge, the older High Street, parish church and river landscapes shaped by the Ouse and Lovat.
perfectFor: A pleasant local-history detour with one genuinely unusual bridge landmark.

suggestedFirstVisit.title: Tickford Bridge and the heritage trail
suggestedFirstVisit.summary: Begin at Tickford Bridge, follow the published heritage route through the old centre, then finish beside the Ouse or in Ousebank Gardens.

dontMiss: St Peter and St Paul Church
